forcedChoices.reason: The authors speak to the readers of Urantia as a group; plural 'you' per the Spanish rules.

forcedChoices.choice: las órdenes (feminine) for orders of beings
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces a gender; the feminine 'orden' carries the sense of a class of beings. 'Órdenes' of motions (15:3.15) stays masculine, the sense of category.
'Running down' and 'winding up' are a clock image; the Spanish clock phrase keeps the pair and the last sentence consistent.
'Plus energy' and 'minus energy' need a noun phrase; positive/negative keeps the sign without more interpretation.
The English uses the short scale; Spanish uses the long scale, so the words change to keep the numbers.
The apposition agrees with 'nebulosas', a feminine noun.
'Understanding personalities' can mean wise or sympathetic; 'comprensivo' keeps both readings open.
The English short-scale trillion (10^12) is the Spanish billón.
The English short-scale billion (10^9) is mil millones in Spanish.

forcedChoices.choice: los seres que representan ... y los que representan ...
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish needs the repeated relative clause to keep the two groups of beings clear.
